title: New Hires on Cooking
summary: I’m thrilled to share that we have three more additions to the New York Times Cooking team: Brooke Caison and Britt Lam, who are joining the social team, and Jill Lubochinski, our first-ever director…
body_markdown:
Brooke Caison, Britt Lam and Jill Lubochinski join The Times. Read more in the below note from Cooking editor Emily Weinstein.


I’m thrilled to share that we have three more additions to the New York Times Cooking team: Brooke Caison and Britt Lam, who are joining the social team, and Jill Lubochinski, our first-ever director of talent strategy. This dynamic and accomplished trio brings our latest round of Cooking newsroom hiring to a close in an extraordinary way.


Photo Credit: Rebecca Simpson-Steele


Brooke Caison is our new social video journalist, with a portfolio that includes hosting vertical videos and recipe development. Working with both the social and recipe teams, Brooke will


pitch, develop and host videos, focusing on instructional content that engages younger audiences and helps them learn to cook. She’ll identify and create original dishes that resonate with a social audience, developing the recipes and occasionally writing as needed.


Brooke comes to us from Delish, where she is currently a senior food editor, a role that encompasses everything from audience and strategy work to video hosting and recipe development. She has also worked as a line cook at several restaurants, as the hospitality manager for Little Island here in New York and as an editorial and culinary assistant to the food writer and television personality Gail Simmons.


Brooke attended culinary school, but she began her career as an engineer; I’m willing to bet that she is the only member of the Cooking editorial team to hold a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering and aviation electronic systems.


She spends her time outside of work sifting through racks at thrift stores, trying to develop a green thumb and perfecting her ideal dirty gin martini recipe.


She starts on Oct. 19 and reports to Becky Hughes.


Photo Credit: Rebecca Simpson-Steele


Pho


Britt Lam is our new senior video journalist for social, working alongside Natasha Janardan to launch and produce vertical video series. Britt will highlight our talent, strengthen our franchises and contribute to the joyful, service-forward video program we’re building.


Britt joins us from The Infatuation, where she played a foundational role in shaping the brand’s video presence on Instagram and TikTok. She scripted, filmed and produced service-oriented pieces about New York restaurants, from


[finding the best chocolate chip cookie in the city](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DJAPNdlyCe-/) to


[eating rice rolls around Chinatown](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DJKEeQSREZ2/) . She eventually grew her scope beyond New York, leading social strategy for tentpole campaigns and managing a global team as director of social content.


Britt started her career as an NBCU page, where she worked on shows like “S.N.L.,” “Late Night with Seth Meyers” and the “Today” show. She lives in Brooklyn, where you can often find her watching the Knicks. Britt starts on Oct. 5, and she also reports to Becky.


Pho


Jill Lubochinski joins us as director of talent strategy, a new senior role in the department. She will work cross-functionally to build a


comprehensive framework for how Cooking works with recipe and video creators, both existing contributors and new ones she’ll help bring in. We work with freelance contributors across every facet of Cooking, and Jill will develop an overarching approach, with an eye toward helping Cooking reach new audiences in a rapidly changing media landscape. She’ll jump in by first taking charge of our creator program.


Jill comes to us from The Washington Post, where she was senior director for creator partnerships and content, a role in which she worked across the newsroom, communications, ad sales, live events and other teams. She led the launch of their creator program, Washington Post Creator, defining strategy, identifying and booking talent, maintaining relationships and building the program’s infrastructure.


Before The Post, Jill was director of entertainment and talent programming for American Express and director of unscripted talent and casting at NBCUniversal. She


is moving back to New York after stints in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C., and she is especially excited to experience the live theater scene here, both on and off Broadway. Jill starts today, and she reports to me.


I’m excited that we have such great new colleagues coming aboard. It’s a testament to the excellence of the work everyone on the team has done so far, and our ambitious vision for our road ahead. And I’m even more excited to see what they’ll do here at The Times.


Please help me welcome Jill, Britt and Brooke!


— Emily
